newsitem.title: USA: U.S. companies more willing to tolerate risks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. companies more willing to tolerate risks.

text.p: ATLANTA, April 16, Reuter - U.S. executives believe their companies face more risk today than they did three years ago, but they are now more willing to tolerate the risk rather than buy insurance coverage, according to a survey sponsored by CIGNA Corp.
The survey, conducted by Wirthlin Worldwide in March and April, gauged the opinions of more than 130 corporate executives.
The survey was released Wednesday at the Risk and Insurance Management Society conference here.
About 38 percent of those polled said they faced somewhat more risk and nearly 16 percent said they faced far greater risks, CIGNA said.
But about 57 percent said their companies were willing to take somewhat greater risk than three years ago and another six percent said they were willing to take far greater risk.
More than 40 percent of companies in the study have taken on more risk by increasing risk retentions or insurance policy deductibles, CIGNA said.
Meanwhile, the greatest worry for the executives was not over catastrophic risk, but economic risk, such as rising interest rates, the survey found.
About 80 percent of the executives said they worried about economic risks but only 40 percent were concerned about catastrophes.

The risk of changing commodity prices, which could affect profit margins, was a concern for about 60 percent of the executives and liability suits and legal settlements were a concern to about 70 percent of the executives.
Half expressed concern about the potential impact of computer-related crimes, CIGNA said.
More companies also are attempting to adopt more sophisticated risk management techniques, the survey showed.
Nearly all the executives said they believed in protecting their company's balance sheet from losses.

A majority of the executives, 68 percent, also said their companies have chosen to self-insure against most risks -- paying for losses out of company assets as they occur -- except for truly catastrophic events.

"In today's environment, companies are taking an enterprise- wide view of risk and seeking solutions designed to protect their overall financial condition," said Dennis Kane, president of Special Risk Facilities for CIGNA Property & Casualty.

"The traditional insurance policy that addresses specific kinds of risks is no longer enough for many firms," he said. "They want risk financing methods focused on reducing the balance-sheet impact of losses whatever their source."
